title: Add benchmark-lab performance suites, profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v126
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds v126 performance test suites and profiling baselines; introduces representative workload runners for multi-turn chat, summarization and reranking; reporting pipeline aggregates results and exports to data warehouse. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We've been iterating on representative workloads and profiling baselines to get more stable per-token cost and latency baselines across our fleet. This PR introduces the v126 performance suites and profiling baselines plus a lightweight reporting pipeline to ingest results from runners and export summarized metrics for dashboards and automated regression detection.

What this PR does: - Adds new benchmark suites that target long-context (~8k) and mixed-length conversational workloads, including: idle profiles, steady-state throughput, cold-start latency, and memory pressure scenarios. - Adds profiling baseline artifacts (serialized traces and flamegraphs) for current kernel selections on our common GPU configs (A100-40GB, H100-80GB) and a default CPU baseline for small-instance runs. - Adds representative workload runners for: multi-turn chat, summarization over long docs, and reranking microbenchmarks. Runners include stable input corpora and deterministic seed handling to make results comparable. - Adds a reporting pipeline that: consumes runner outputs (JSON+tar artifacts), normalizes metrics, calculates percentiles / token-efficiency metrics, and writes summarized rows to our benchmarking BigQuery dataset and a metrics topic used by the console. Pipeline includes schema validation, retention policy, and lightweight deduplication.

Checklist: - [x] Benchmarks implemented and smoke-tested locally - [x] Profiling baselines uploaded to internal artifact store - [x] Reporting pipeline ETL tested with sample payloads - [x] CI integration (unit + integration) passing - [x] Docs README for running the suites and adding new workloads

Context & rationale: This change is driven by ongoing regressions we observed in the serving runtime after kernel swaps; having a canonical v126 baseline lets us detect regressions earlier in PR gates and on release canaries. The reporting pipeline standardizes outputs so dashboards and regression alerts can reliably consume the same fields. Related: ENG-1287 (benchmarking infra improvements), ENG-1302 (profiling baselines lifecycle).

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please add a short note about how seeds are managed for deterministic runs. Also we should avoid storing raw trace payloads long-term - prefer aggregated artifacts.

Priya Nair (author): Added percentile unit test and updated compute_metrics to use inclusive percentile definition per telemetry team guidance.

changelog_summary: Added benchmark-lab v126 performance suites, profiling baselines for A100/H100 and CPU, representative workload runners (chat/summarize/rerank), and a reporting pipeline that normalizes and exports benchmark summaries to BigQuery and metrics topics. No breaking API changes.
